clue.text: Fruit added to pile in rhyme

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a rick is a stack or pile, especially of hay

explanation.surface: Someone stacks fruit on a heap while reciting verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-line comic verse with a fixed scheme is a kind of rhyme, so the form fits the broad word.

clue.text: Hang around in underwear? That's out

indicators.note: out says the letters for the words that's leave the underwear word

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear
i.e. (id est) is read as 'that is'

explanation.surface: A coy question about loitering in one's underwear, answered with a dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is the abbreviation IE (Latin id est, 'that is'); 'out' removes it from LINGERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay about or dawdle, which is what hanging around means.

clue.text: Do one's bit, bringing manure home

parts.note: muck is dung or manure
in means at home

explanation.surface: A gardener does their share by bringing fertiliser back to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To muck in is the idiom for sharing work and pulling one's weight.

clue.text: Letter about city on the sea, and place on the Thames

indicators.note: about says the letter word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an old Germanic alphabet
NY is New York
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A letter mentions a coastal city and a riverside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the letter round the city and sea together. Runnymede is the Thames-side meadow where Magna Carta was sealed in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: Runnymede is a meadow beside the Thames in Surrey, so it is a riverside place.

clue.text: Fail to discover missing boat with cloth put over

indicators.note: missing says the boat letters are absent from the phrase for discover

parts.note: to come across something is to discover it
SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: in a down clue, put over means the cloth word is turned upwards

parts.note: repp, also spelt rep, is a ribbed fabric

explanation.surface: Someone loses a boat and covers the gap with a sheet, a failure all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops the steamship; 'put over' turns the cloth upwards in this down light. Repp is a less familiar spelling of rep, the ribbed fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is the idiom for falling heavily, and so for failing badly.

clue.text: Heading for London, going on to Paddington, keep cheerful

indicators.note: going on to says the London piece follows the bear

parts.note: Paddington is the children's-book bear
one goes up to London, the traditional direction toward the capital

explanation.surface: A traveller heads for London, continuing to Paddington station, and stays upbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London station, but here it is Paddington Bear; travel to London is traditionally 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is to stay brave and cheerful in difficulty.

clue.text: Show I have retreated before an army

indicators.note: retreated means the words for I have go backwards, upwards in this down clue

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have
TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: Someone reports falling back ahead of an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreated' turns IVE into EVI. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical, an example of a show.

clue.text: Fortified wine, ruby — put order in

annotationWithheld.why: Fortified wine, ruby — put order in (3,5): RED BIDDY; scan agrees, but no parse found: removing BID (order) leaves REDDY, which 'ruby' does not give
annotationWithheld.clue: Fortified wine, ruby — put order in

clue.text: Chap confined in small room — it's formality

indicators.note: confined in says the chap is shut inside the room

parts.note: a pantry is a small room for food
Ed is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man is shut up in a little room, which is a formal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive attention to rules and form, so it suits formality.

clue.text: Sobriquet — Dartmoor, for instance?

definitions.meaning: a sobriquet is an informal name given to a person
Dartmoor is the name of a famous prison, and a prison is a nick in slang

explanation.surface: A nickname compared to a moorland place name.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for prison; Dartmoor is a well-known prison in Devon, so its name is a nick name.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal name for a person is a sobriquet, the dictionary sense.

clue.text: Wife really short of energy, and short of breath

indicators.note: short of says the energy letter is dropped from the word for really

parts.note: indeed means really
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A wife lacks energy and is puffed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being winded means having the breath knocked out, so short of breath.

clue.text: Hazardous job in which Bob's diplomas could be utilised

indicators.note: the letters could be put to use in a new order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the name with its S is taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Bob's qualifications might be put to use in a dangerous line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'could be utilised' rearranges BOBS DIPLOMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Defusing and removing explosives is notoriously dangerous work, a hazardous job.

clue.text: Change for the better? I defy change

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of I defy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resists being reformed, defiantly refusing change.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'change' is the anagram signal for I DEFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to improve someone morally or intellectually.

clue.text: Worship — a fellow accepts a certain proportion

indicators.note: accepts says the fellow takes the proportion inside him

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
a ratio is a fixed proportion

explanation.surface: A college fellow takes on a fixed share of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts the proportion inside the fellow, not at his end: it sits between his second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and reverence, as given in worship.

clue.text: Cowboy joins Gerald and Bob

parts.note: Jerry is a pet form of Gerald
Bob the Builder is a children's TV character

explanation.surface: A cowboy teams up with two men named Gerald and Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowboy' is the British sense, a shoddy, unscrupulous tradesman, not a ranch hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a cowboy is a dodgy tradesman, and a jerry-builder puts up cheap, flimsy houses.

clue.text: Information concealed by Eskimo with unknown invention

indicators.note: concealed by says the information is hidden inside the Eskimo word

parts.note: Inuit are Arctic people once called Eskimos
gen is British slang for information
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An Arctic hunter hides information about an unknown invention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuity is inventiveness, cleverness in devising things.

clue.text: Old man's 26 papers

parts.note: pa is father, the old man, so pa's
26 points to 26-across, whose verb sense is to play or toy; sport means the same

explanation.surface: Father's documents, cross-referenced to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 26-across answer as a verb means toy or play, which is also what sport means.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an identity document, the papers one shows at a border.

clue.text: Daughter of Middle Eastern country's PM

parts.note: Israeli means of Israel, a Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: The daughter of a Middle Eastern nation's prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister: Benjamin Disraeli led Britain in 1868 and 1874-80.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli was a Victorian British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Girl's power extends all round town down under

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name, so Alice's
P is the symbol for power
rings means encircles, goes all round

explanation.surface: A girl's influence spreads around an Australian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in Australia's Northern Territory, down under being slang for Australia.

clue.text: Lizard — one moving northward in part of S America

indicators.note: in a down clue northward means toward the top, so the one moves to the front

parts.note: Guiana is a region of northern South America
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lizard climbs north through part of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in GUIANA moves to the top of the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

clue.text: Appear in the nude — not how skater is normally seen

indicators.note: not how and is normally seen together say the letters are not in their usual order
this completes the signal that the word skater is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone appears naked, unlike the usual sight of a skater.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place.

clue.text: Waste paper — cash can be made from it

definitions.text: Waste paper — cash can be made from it

indicators.note: waste suggests spoiling the words so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Recycling scrap paper can bring in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' is the anagram signal for PAPER CASH, and the whole clue describes a junk pile that can be sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded material is something from which money can be made by selling scrap.

clue.text: Search for prey by predatory creature after half prey goes missing

indicators.note: after places the creature behind the remaining letters
half says only the first two of the four letters of prey are kept

parts.note: an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A predator searches for prey, having lost half its quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prey' appears twice: once in the definition, once as the word halved; 'after' puts the bird behind the remaining half.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move stealthily in search of prey.

clue.text: Thing suffering damage when it's dark

indicators.note: damage to the word thing breaks its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Something gets damaged after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time when it is dark.

clue.text: Old Scot, perhaps, giving home to old cat

parts.note: O again for old

indicators.note: giving home to says the Scot houses the second old

parts.note: a Scot is an example of a Celt
O again for old

explanation.surface: An elderly Scot shelters an aging cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Sounded with an H, like Hook

parts.note: as means like
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Something pronounced with an H, like the name Hook.
explanation.walkthrough: Hook does begin with H, which is the false trail; he is Captain Hook, a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspirate a sound is to pronounce it with an audible breath, as an H.

clue.text: Play with dessert

definitions.meaning: a layered pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with is to toy with, and the British pudding of sponge, custard and cream shares the name.

clue.text: Listen to recording, and refund about a pound

indicators.note: about says the refund goes round the pound

parts.note: a payback is a repayment, a refund
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone hears a recording and gets their money back.
explanation.definitionFit: To play back a recording is to replay it so as to listen to it.
